name: Iowa Admin. Code 567-63.6(455B) Bypasses and upsets (incl. public notices)
operator: Iowa Department of Natural Resources / Iowa Legislature
status_reason: Regulator report by phone within 24 hours, written report within 5 days; a public notice only if DNR decides one is necessary.
notes: 63.6(3) Notification of unanticipated bypass or upset and public notices (PNs). In the event that a bypass or upset occurs without prior notice having been provided pursuant to 63.6(2) or as a result of mechanical failure or acts beyond the control of the owner or operator, the owner or operator of the treatment facility or collection system shall notify the department by telephone as soon as possible but not later than 24 hours after the onset or discovery. ... c. Upon notification, the department shall determine if a PN for an unanticipated bypass is necessary. If the department determines that a PN is necessary, the owner or operator of the treatment facility or the collection system shall prepare a PN. 63.6(1): "Bypasses from any portion of a treatment facility or from a sanitary sewer collection system designed to carry only sewage are prohibited."

name: Iowa DNR news releases on wastewater bypasses and discharges
waters_covered: statewide, events DNR chooses to announce
access_detail: Drupal list of dated releases (/news-release/YYYY-MM-DD/slug), 13 on the first page on 2026-11-03; no RSS found (/rss.xml and /news-releases/rss.xml 404). Sample: raw/ia-dnr-news-keokuk-2026-08-04.html. Older releases under /advisories/ (e.g. 2024-08-01 "heavy rains lead wastewater bypasses central and southern iowa").

sample_record.title: Wastewater discharge in Keokuk reaches Mississippi River
sample_record.text: The wastewater is being discharged through a combined sewer outfall into the Mississippi River, located east of the wastewater treatment plant. This outfall is situated upstream from the public boat ramp along Mississippi Drive. It is unknown how much wastewater has been discharged at this time. ... Downstream recreational users should take caution and avoid the area at this time.

cadence: Event-driven, at DNR's discretion; Keokuk notice came about a week after the bypass began.
license: State of Iowa site policies; not quoted.
status_reason: The only statewide, dated public channel for bypasses, but discretionary and sparse; needs a list poller and a keyword filter.

name: Iowa DNR Field Office Compliance database: Spill Search
access_detail: Public search (anti-forgery token + cookie) POST /focomp/Search/SpillSearch; export endpoint /focomp/Search/SpillSearchExport. Material filter has "Municipal wastewater" (2786), "Wastewater (domestic)" (2110). 2024-01-01 to 2026-11-03: 2 municipal wastewater and 5 domestic wastewater spills (e.g. 2024-08-28 Des Moines River & Kenyon Road, Webster County, 400,000 gallons; 2024-09-18 Nashua STP, 16,000 gallons). October 2026: 27 spills, none sewage.
cadence: Entered by field staff; records since about 2009.
status_reason: Sewage bypasses are mostly not filed as spills (7 sewage rows in three years); staff names appear in results and must never be stored.
notes: Results include a staff-name column; drop it on ingest. Name-free extract of the 2024-2026 sewage rows: raw/ia-spillsearch-sewage-sanitized.csv.

name: Iowa DNR AQuIA beach monitoring (weekly E. coli and microcystin, advisories)
waters_covered: State park beaches (about 40) and county/city beaches
access_detail: JSON API /aquia/api/v1/beaches/weekly_results/state?week=all and /countycity?week=all (empty [] off season); CSV /aquia/Programs/DownloadBeachResults/State with header siteID,name,beachClassification,owner,sampleDate,week,eColi,eColi5wGeomean,microcystin,status,comments; /aquia/api/v1/beaches/reference/statuses. Site pages /aquia/Sites/{siteID}.
cadence: Updated Fridays, Memorial Day to Labor Day; hotline 515-725-3434.
status_reason: Clean JSON/CSV with both E. coli and microcystin; thresholds 235 CFU/100 mL and 8 ug/L.
